---
title: "Learning paths"
---

The materials are modular: there is no requirement to work through them in a fixed order. These suggested paths show how resources could be combined.

## Understanding published syntheses

For decision makers, practitioners and students who need to interpret reviews:

1. Framing an answerable question *(planned)*
2. Recognising study designs and threats to validity *(planned)*
3. [Understanding effect sizes](modules/effect-sizes.qmd)
4. Reading a forest plot *(planned)*
5. Judging heterogeneity and applicability *(planned)*

## Conducting an evidence synthesis

For learners planning or undertaking a review:

1. Questions and eligibility criteria *(planned)*
2. Searching and screening *(planned)*
3. Critical appraisal *(planned)*
4. Data extraction and effect-size calculation *(planned)*
5. Quantitative or narrative synthesis *(planned)*
6. Reporting and reproducibility *(planned)*

## Short methods workshop

For a half-day introductory session:

1. What makes evidence trustworthy? *(planned)*
2. [Understanding effect sizes](modules/effect-sizes.qmd)
3. Interpreting a forest plot *(planned)*
4. A critical-appraisal exercise *(planned)*
